label: input token u
explanation: Single-token detector: fires whenever the current input is the letter u, in any position, in both the original phase and the copy phase (where u is fed back). Nearly every u input activates it (dev: precision 1.0, recall 0.99995). Strongest when u is the first token (t=0, about 0.97 of max). u inputs elsewhere sit around 0.63-0.85 of max; in the dev examples the top step is a u right before <DEL>. Never fires on any other token (5 stray activations each on g and 2) or on the delimiter step. Position, L, and the output target do not decide whether it fires.

issues: No systematic counterexamples found. On test, 0 false positives and 11 missed activations that carry 0.0% of the mass. Every miss is a weak (about 0.15 of max) activation at step 8 (L=9, the last original token) on the input g or 2. That is scattered noise, not a token class: g and 2 are almost never active elsewhere (5 of about 199k each on dev).

The fire rate on u inputs is 1.000 in the original phase and in the copy phase. The delimiter step never fires. Position, L, out_tok and prev_tok all have lift of about 1.0 or less, so none of them decides whether it fires.

The magnitude claims hold: u at t=0 is 0.97 of max. Other u inputs sit at about 0.63-0.87 of max, and the dev max of 1.00 is a u right before <DEL>. One small nuance is that copy-phase activations are slightly weaker than original-phase ones (share of mass 0.438 vs 0.562 on similar counts). This doesn't affect the label.
